Keep planning evidence from the worker's separate commit

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 3, Harm 4
Raise: Data loss
Case: normal use - a teammate clones a squashed stacked part and a reviewer repeats a dismissed finding whose cited line is unchanged.
`squash_replay` copies review-state snapshots without retaining the original commits referenced by their `review.commit` fields (`src/forge/close_remote.py:47`). The published start tag points to the initial commit, not the later reviewed commits (`src/forge/task.py:297`). In a fresh network clone, `review._cited_changed` treats its failed diff against the missing commit as a changed citation (`src/forge/review.py:666`), so `review.run` does not carry the dismissal and close can block on the settled finding again. The new test checks that the reason appears in the prompt but does not repeat the finding.
findings.title: Preserve earlier review rounds during the squash

why: When a stacked part's parent has merged, close replays the part's own commits onto main one by one (git rebase in close._merge_default), so an early commit conflicts with later main edits of the same lines even when the whole-branch merge is clean; merging main into the branch never helps, and a client part looped 5 times on 19 Nov 2026
